PullRequest.Title: linux: add launcher migration notices and shortcut sanity checks
PullRequest.Body:
Related to #337589.

## Problem

#332935 renamed the DEB/RPM desktop entry IDs in 1.139.0. Existing favorites, pinned launchers, and saved desktop/MIME references can still point at the removed filenames.

## Changes

- Keep only the canonical reverse-DNS application entry and hidden URL handler. **Do not ship legacy desktop files or an additional application shortcut.** Saved references require manual migration.
- Add a compressed Debian `NEWS.Debian` notice and RPM `%doc` NEWS, both linking to the release-note migration guidance. Debian frontends using apt-listchanges can display NEWS; this depends on the user's installation/configuration. RPM NEWS is packaged documentation, not a guaranteed upgrade notification.
- Use a fixed Debian NEWS version newer than the affected Stable package (`1.139.0-1790100840`), rather than generating a new entry for every build.
- Keep desktop generation shared within the existing Linux packaging gulpfile. Snap packaging is unchanged.

## Release sanity coverage

- **DEB/RPM:** validate the canonical application and hidden URL-handler entries, executable targets, application window identity, handler arguments/MIME type, and visibility. Exercise the one application entry's parsed `Exec` command by opening a unique file in the isolated test window. These container checks do not require GTK/GIO or a full desktop shell and do not simulate saved favorites.
- **Windows installers:** explicitly request the Desktop shortcut, validate Start Menu and Desktop `.lnk` targets in the appropriate user/common folders, and exercise the shortcuts through ShellExecute.
- **macOS bundles:** validate executable/type metadata and exercise LaunchServices with the exact downloaded ZIP/DMG bundle.
- Preserve download-only behavior and archive/server exclusions. Snap retains direct-launch coverage. Keep installer/DMG cleanup on failures.

## Companion release notes

microsoft/vscode-docs#10378 documents the breaking change and manual migration. **Publish it before packages containing the notices ship**, so their link resolves:
https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_139#_linux-desktop-launcher-names

## Validation

- Build tooling typecheck, sanity compile, targeted ESLint, and whitespace checks passed.
- Exercised the actual desktop/NEWS generation streams for Stable, Insiders, and OSS: two canonical desktop entries and the expected notice paths.
- Parsed rendered Debian NEWS and verified version ordering and matching release-note links.
- Built and inspected a minimal DEB fixture with native `dpkg-deb`, confirming the generated compressed NEWS and exactly two canonical desktop files survive packaging.
- Previously verified Windows shortcut argument forwarding and uninstall cleanup for all four installer registrations when post-install validation fails.

Full installed-product sanity runs across Linux, Windows, and macOS, native RPM packaging, and a real KDE upgrade remain release/CI validation; they were not run locally.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build and package Linux DEB/RPM artifacts, then install or upgrade them
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing dependency scan/sysroot resolution completes first, then packaging merges product files with one new NEWS file; Debian additionally gzip-compresses that small file before dpkg-deb, while RPM copies it before rpmbuild. End-user application startup does not consume either NEWS file; Debian frontends may read it during package upgrade.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read one fixed-size NEWS source and write one documentation file into each package staging tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one source read and one staged output per DEB or RPM artifact; three architecture task definitions exist, but each artifact gets one file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The package preparation stream did not read or emit a NEWS document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds constant, tiny filesystem work to package preparation; it must finish before package assembly.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Gzip the fixed eight-line Debian NEWS file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per DEB artifact with input under 1 KB.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs on the package-preparation critical path but has constant negligible CPU/allocation cost.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan native modules and resolve/extract build sysroots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing once-per-package dependency generation; Chromium metadata is fetched each DEB preparation, while sysroot archives use stamp-file caches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical dependency and sysroot work already preceded construction of the packaging streams.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can dominate cold package preparation, but the diff neither adds nor increases these calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assemble the staged tree with dpkg-deb or rpmbuild.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same package assembly subprocess ran without the NEWS file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required after staging; the added tiny document does not change subprocess cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed template size and one document per artifact, independent of repository size, installed extensions, user data, or package history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within each prepare task, vinyl streams are merged, but only one NEWS item is added. Architecture/package tasks are independently scheduled by the external build pipeline; the diff introduces no new parallel subprocesses or unbounded queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new NEWS transformation has no cache and is repeated once per artifact. Existing sysroot stamp caches preserve warm behavior; the diff does not change their keys or invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete packaging hunks and task registrations: the only new work is one tiny stream item per artifact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact filesystem and compressor timings vary by builder, but the added input is only a few hundred bytes and fixed-cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: constant-size documentation I/O/compression is negligible beside existing package assembly and does not affect application runtime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run installed Linux DEB/RPM desktop sanity tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing package-manager install and main Playwright UI test, the test synchronously invokes the canonical desktop command once, then waits for one unique file tab before app teardown and package uninstall.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install and uninstall the tested package with dpkg or rpm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One install and one uninstall per selected package test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same package-manager calls surrounded the desktop app test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing dominant test setup/cleanup boundaries; launcher validation runs between them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read product.json and two desktop entries, check executable access, and resolve executable paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three small file reads plus bounded metadata checks per installed artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The sanity test launched the installed executable directly without validating installed desktop files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before Electron launch, but does not scale with workspace or package contents.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the application desktop entry with isolated directories and --reuse-window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launcher subprocess per installed DEB/RPM test; the URL-handler entry is parsed but not launched.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No additional launcher subprocess or tab wait followed the main UI test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous command must return and one editor tab must appear before teardown; successful reuse hands off to the existing app, while the 30-second process/tab limits bound failure cost.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One launcher execution per installed artifact selected by host OS/architecture, not per desktop entry, file collection, or user workspace item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mocha has no parallel option enabled, package tests run serially, and the launcher loop awaits each tab before continuing. There is no aggregate process burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is added. Reads may benefit from the OS page cache after install, but behavior and call count are the same on cold and warm runs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from test registration, default serial Mocha configuration, and the single-element Linux launcher array.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Launcher handoff latency depends on the CI host; successful work is one bounded reuse-window request, and long waits occur only on failure.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the additional boundary is intentional release validation, fixed-cardinality, serial, and bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run Windows installer and shortcut sanity tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The installer now creates the requested desktop shortcut; after existing signature scans, one PowerShell call resolves two shortcuts, then two shortcut launches and tab waits run sequentially before uninstall.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the existing installer to create one desktop shortcut in addition to its normal Start Menu shortcut.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra .lnk creation per installer test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Silent installation explicitly disabled app launch but did not request the optional desktop icon.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the installer subprocess critical path; fixed-size metadata write.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run PowerShell once to resolve and inspect Start Menu and Desktop shortcuts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One PowerShell process returning two fixed shortcut records per installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before Electron starts and must complete successfully.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use PowerShell Start-Process to open each .lnk and wait for the corresponding tab in the already-running application.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly two serial launcher processes and two serial waits per installer artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The app was launched directly once for UI testing; shortcuts were neither created nor exercised.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds launcher validation to the test critical path, bounded by 30-second process and tab timeouts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One install and one uninstall per selected Windows installer test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same installer lifecycle ran without shortcut probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing dominant setup/cleanup work; shortcut creation is a bounded installer task flag.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two known shortcuts per installer, across the host-compatible user/system installer artifacts; no dependence on profile contents or project size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mocha executes tests serially and the launcher loop waits after each shortcut, so at most one PowerShell launcher probe is active at a time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cross-test cache or coalescing is used or needed for two fixed records. OS shortcut/application caches may be warm, but call cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the fixed two-folder array, two-record assertion, serial loop, and serial Mocha options.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: PowerShell startup cost varies on CI, but the maximum successful multiplicity is two launches per tested installer and there is no fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: CI duration increases by a small, deliberate, bounded number of subprocesses with no concurrency burst or product runtime impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run macOS archive and DMG desktop sanity tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each host-compatible bundle, two PlistBuddy reads run before Electron launch; after the existing UI test, one /usr/bin/open launcher request and one tab wait complete before app close. DMG unmount now runs in finally on failures.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke PlistBuddy twice to read bundle executable and package type.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two fixed metadata subprocesses per tested macOS bundle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The sanity test codesign-validated and directly launched the bundle without these metadata subprocesses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serial pre-launch checks on the test critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke LaunchServices through /usr/bin/open and wait for a unique file tab.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process and one serial wait per tested bundle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No LaunchServices probe followed the direct Electron launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the UI test and before teardown, bounded by 30-second process and tab timeouts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mount and unmount DMG volumes, with unmount moved into finally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mount and one unmount per selected DMG test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful runs performed the same unmount, but failures before the old unmount could leave the volume mounted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing lifecycle boundaries; the changed placement prevents mounts from surviving validation failures rather than adding successful-path work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One LaunchServices probe and two metadata reads per host-compatible archive/DMG bundle; independent of bundle file count and user data size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Default Mocha execution is serial, each bundle performs fixed metadata calls synchronously, and only one launcher is returned, so no process burst occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No explicit cache; fixed Info.plist reads may hit the OS cache. DMG/archive selection does not create repeated per-file work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the one-element launcher array, synchronous helper calls, serial test runner, and finally blocks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Process startup and LaunchServices handoff latency vary by machine; multiplicity remains fixed and timeout-bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added sanity coverage is bounded and serial, while the cleanup change improves failure-path resource lifetime.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review over all eight changed files and all diff pages. The PR adds only constant-size package documentation work and fixed-cardinality, serial launcher-validation subprocesses in release sanity tests; it introduces no hot product path, unbounded retention, fan-out, or concurrency burst, so no findings were submitted.
